quantity: Rayleigh speed for an incompressible solid, squared
inputs: Incompressible half-space, lambda = infinity (h^2 = 0); cubic (25) k^6 - 8k^4 + 24k^2 - 16 = 0
how_source_obtained_it: real root of the printed cubic (25); Rayleigh gives the root numerically and factorises (k^2 - .91275)(k^4 - 7.08725k^2 + 17.5311) = 0
notes: The wave speed follows as 0.9554 sqrt(mu/rho) (p.9).

quantity: Surface wave speed for an incompressible solid
inputs: Same incompressible case; p/f with k = .9554 f (eq (32))
how_source_obtained_it: closed form from eq (26) and (32): p/f = .9554 sqrt(mu/rho)
notes: Printed as 'rather more slowly' than transverse waves.

quantity: Attenuation exponents for the two-dimensional incompressible case
inputs: Incompressible, propagation along x (g = 0), k = .9554 f
how_source_obtained_it: closed form from the roots of (26) and (12),(17)
notes: s is the decay exponent of the complementary part.

quantity: Depth at which the horizontal displacement vanishes
inputs: Two-dimensional surface wave, wavelength lambda' = 2 pi/f
how_source_obtained_it: closed form from the printed amplitude ratio .5433 in eq (33)
notes: 'there is no finite depth at which the vertical motion vanishes'.

inputs: Table of the paper; columns lambda/mu and Poisson ratio (headings not recoverable from the text layer)
how_source_obtained_it: table computed by the author from eq (24); no formula for the individual entries is printed
notes: OCR of the table's column headings is lost; the value .9127 agrees with eq (25) and .9554 with eq (32). The text layer also shows a leading 0 and a 1 in the h^2 column whose row alignment cannot be fixed from the scan, so only the four aligned rows are reported. Manual check of the table layout required.

quantity: Wave speed on a layered half-space (Rayleigh type)
inputs: fT = 6, s/f = .25, rho' = rho (layer on half-space, incompressible treatment)
printed_value: V = (.9682) b, with b = sqrt(mu/rho); mu'/mu = 2.325 and W = 2.65
units: speed as a multiple of b; rigidity ratio dimensionless
how_source_obtained_it: numerical root of the approximate frequency equation (67) reduced to a quadratic in W, printed p.172
notes: Compared by the author with the simple Rayleigh value (.9553) b, i.e. about 1 per cent higher.

quantity: Rayleigh wave velocity from rock constants
inputs: Rigidity 2.5e11 dyn/cm^2, density 2.8 g/cm^3, formula 0.9 sqrt(mu/rho)
how_source_obtained_it: approximation, explicitly 'expressed by the formula 0.9 sqrt(mu/rho)'
notes: Order-of-magnitude estimate used to compare with observed arrivals.

quantity: Stoneley wave speed for a density contrast
inputs: rho1 = 8.2, rho2 = 3.2 (Wiechert density law), incompressible media, beta1 = beta2 = beta
units: speed as a multiple of beta
how_source_obtained_it: root of the printed sextic (3), obtained numerically by the author
notes: Velocity 'very slightly less than that of distortional waves in either medium'.

quantity: Rejected complex root of the same sextic
how_source_obtained_it: numerical root of (3), then tested with the decay condition (7)
notes: Printed and then discarded: the complex roots are inadmissible because the two attenuations cannot both decay.

quantity: Extraneous roots from the squared equation
inputs: rho1 = 2, rho2 = 1, beta2^2 = (2/3) beta1^2, x = c/beta1
how_source_obtained_it: roots of eq (11) obtained numerically; the author then substitutes back into (1) of section 3
notes: Neither root satisfies the original equation; they satisfy it only with the sign of one side changed, and are therefore not physical modes.

quantity: Homogeneous Bleustein-Gulyaev speeds and coupling for PZT-4
how_source_obtained_it: closed form from (3.16), (3.18) and the coupling definition (3.22) evaluated on the printed PZT-4 constants
notes: A later script can reproduce all three from the four material constants; the paper states the approximation in (3.22) is justified for PZT-4.

quantity: Upper bound on the inhomogeneity strength beta/k
inputs: Exponential profile f = exp(-2 beta x2), metalized surface, chi^2 from the PZT-4 constants
how_source_obtained_it: closed form derived from the decay requirement 2 beta/k < q1 - beta/k with q1 from (3.23)
notes: Threshold at which the inhomogeneity decays more slowly than the displacement; beyond it the decay argument fails.
